evals.name: pin-shop-customer-and-invite
evals.prompt: Write only a Screenplay specification excerpt for the shop's RegisterCustomer. It has customerId CustomerId generated identifier and inviteCode InviteCode generated. CustomerId is String with generate ulid prefix cus_ and InviteCode uses generate nanoid. Inline CustomerRegistered carries inviteCode and targets customerId; returns has customerId and inviteCode. Pin customerId to cus_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV and inviteCode to abcdefghijklmnopqrstu. Do not change the command or turn generated properties into inputs.
evals.expected_output: specification RegistersWithPinnedValues with when RegisterCustomer, indented for "cus_01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV" and generated inviteCode = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstu"; then CustomerRegistered with its own for and complete inviteCode payload; then returns with customerId and inviteCode matching the same pins. Both pins match v15 shapes; no seed/request mapping is introduced.
assertions: Pins the generated CustomerId with indented for beneath when, not an input property or a generated customerId fixture.
Pins InviteCode using generated inviteCode = with the exact 21-symbol NanoID value.
States the expected event's own destination and complete inviteCode payload.
Asserts both named response fields against the same whole-value pins without changing the command.

evals.name: clock-does-not-draw-shop-identifiers
evals.prompt: On Screenplay 4.151.0 our shop's PlaceOrder uses a TypeID OrderId generated identifier and an event's $context.occurred. I set given clock to 2026-10-05T08:00:00Z and a random seed but omitted the identifier pin. Will the reference evaluator create the same OrderId and pass? We also want a secret ApiKey generation spec matching .NET Bytes(32). How should we specify this, and what differs on Stage 4.89.1? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: given clock supplies $context.occurred, not a generated TypeID. Pin the whole OrderId with for and other generated values by name; seeds are not portable fixtures. Reaching unpinned generation is Unsupported(IdentityAllocation), not pass. Preserve ApiKey secret and report generation as unadmitted, not a successful issuance spec. Stage Debug specs can use AllowGeneration with supported relational assertions but its in-memory executor requires pins; its time-ordered factories use wall clock, not Arc receipt-time/tenant context, and clock specs are refused.
assertions: Separates given clock's occurred timestamp from generated OrderId and rejects seed-based portable fixtures.
Requires the whole identifier pin via for, reporting missing reference fixtures as Unsupported rather than passed.
Preserves ApiKey's secret contract without inventing a passing generated-secret specification.
Distinguishes Stage Debug relational generation from deterministic reference/in-memory requirements, wall-clock factories and unsupported clock specs.

evals.name: strict-shop-fixtures-and-source-freshness
evals.prompt: Our v15 shop model uses generate typeid order for OrderId. A success spec pins it to order_00000000000000000000000000 (a zero UUID suffix, not v7/RFC-variant). Another pins a valid TypeID whose whole source already has prior facts on another stream. Should either pass, should the runner retry, and would a pin prove authorization or randomness? Compare older implicit-UUID models without serialized generation. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: The invalid TypeID pin is a v15 Contract rejection because the UUID suffix does not have the required version/variant. The valid reused source yields whole-command Concurrency with no append or response and no silent retry regardless of stream/event type. Serialized generation selects v15 guarding all generated destinations. Older implicit-UUID models retain canonical-only checks and unguarded reuse; removing the TypeID strategy is not an equivalent older model. Pins demonstrate deterministic behavior, not entropy, authorization, idempotency or target storage correctness.
assertions: Rejects the invalid TypeID suffix as a v15 Contract failure, not client validation.
Reports existing whole-source facts as Concurrency with no append/response or silent retry even on another stream.
Explains v15 guard selection versus historical implicit-UUID unguarded models, without treating strategy removal as equivalent behavior.
Does not treat pins as proof of randomness, authorization, idempotency or target storage correctness.
